children: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJI) extended its recent retreat on Wednesday, falling 0.5% to its lowest level in more than a month.

The blue-chip index has now moved 4.2% below its record high of 54,744.33, reached earlier this year. The decline follows a broader pullback as investors reassess equities after an extended period of gains.
Market pressure has also intensified across major U.S. indexes. The Dow fell 1.2% on Tuesday to 52,786.07, while the S&P 500 dropped 0.6% and the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.3%.
Wednesday's weakness came as investors dealt with renewed inflation concerns tied to higher oil prices and geopolitical tensions.
Brent crude moved above $100 a barrel, while Treasury yields remained elevated, adding another source of pressure for stocks.
Despite the recent losses, the Dow remains higher for the year. Investors are now watching economic data and developments in energy markets for clues on whether the pullback could persist.

title: Dow Hits 1-Month Low as Oil Surges Above $100
